map.通过光圈、快门、ISO 计算曝光值（EV），并进行等效曝光互易律换算: Compute exposure value (EV) from aperture, shutter and ISO, and perform equivalent-exposure reciprocity conversion.
map.EV₁₀₀ = log₂(N²/t) − log₂(S/100)；绝对曝光值 E: EV100 = log2(N^2/t) - log2(S/100); absolute exposure EV = log2(N^2/t); equivalent shutter t = 100*N^2/(S*2^EV100)
map.N 为光圈 f 值，t 为快门时间(s)，S 为 ISO。EV₁₀₀ 归一到 I: N is the aperture f-number, t is shutter time (s), S is ISO. EV100 normalized to ISO 100 eases cross-sensitivity comparison; each 1 EV difference means double light. Scene brightness graded by EV100 (snowy noon >=16, Sunny 16 rule ~14, cloudy ~12, night <=2).
map.💡 EV₁₀₀ = log₂(N²/t) − log₂(ISO/100)；保持: 💡 EV100 = log2(N^2/t) - log2(ISO/100); keeping EV unchanged, opening aperture 1 stop needs shutter 1 stop faster
map.输入目标 EV 与任意两项（第三项留空自动求解）: Enter target EV and any two items (leave the third blank to auto-solve)
map.快门支持分数（1/125）、小数（0.008）或整数（2）秒: Shutter accepts fraction (1/125), decimal (0.008) or integer (2) seconds
map.EV100 为 ISO100 基准下的曝光值，反映场景亮度（如日光约 EV15）: EV100 is the exposure value at ISO 100 baseline, reflecting scene brightness (e.g. daylight ~EV15)
map.互易律在极长/极短曝光下可能失效，实际拍摄以实测为准: Reciprocity may fail at very long/short exposures; real shooting relies on measurement
map.调整光圈、快门、ISO 三要素平衡曝光。: Balance exposure by adjusting aperture, shutter and ISO three factors.
map.计算 EV 值并给出等效曝光组合。: Compute EV and give equivalent exposure combos.
map.按 EV 判断场景亮度等级。: Judge scene brightness level by EV.
map.把光圈从 f/8 收到 f/11、或快门加快一档，曝光减少 1 EV；需相应提高: Stop aperture from f/8 to f/11, or speed shutter 1 stop, reduces exposure by 1 EV; compensate by raising ISO or slowing shutter.
map.晴天约 EV100≈15，可用 f/16 + 1/100s + ISO100 获: Sunny day ~EV100 15, use f/16 + 1/100s + ISO100 for roughly correct exposure.
map.光圈、快门与 ISO 三者共同决定曝光量，任一变化都会改变亮度与画面风格（景深、: Aperture, shutter and ISO together decide exposure; any change alters brightness and image style (depth of field, motion, noise).
map.EV 值越大画面越亮吗？: Does larger EV mean brighter image?
map.EV 描述场景亮度与曝光组合，数值越小代表光线越暗、需要越多曝光量。: EV describes scene brightness and exposure combo; smaller value means darker light, more exposure needed.
